label: explicit_exclusion
rationale: DSRCT is expressly listed under tumor types that will not be included. Permission to discuss unlisted types does not override a named exclusion.
cohort_reconciliation: The completed safety run-in and randomized trabectedin versus trabectedin/tTF-NGR portion use the same stated histologic scope. No DSRCT exception is stated in either arm.
extra_biomarker_requirement: Central CD13 positivity is required for eligible tumor types, but does not nullify the explicit DSRCT exclusion.
protocol_uncertainty: External protocol is unreviewed; saved narrative reports randomized-part opening, but current sites/slots are not independently verified. No safety inference is made from the registry's run-in discussion.
quotes: The following tumor types will not be included:
Tumor types not listed above may be included upon communication with Coordinating Investigator.

label: explicit_diagnosis_compatible
rationale: Adult inclusion explicitly names DSRCT despite SCLC-focused title and conditions. This is diagnostic imaging scope, not therapeutic eligibility.
cohort_reconciliation: Adult criteria admit DSRCT at age at least 18; pediatric criteria are separately restricted to high-risk neuroblastoma. Both listed phase arms specify at least 50% DLL3-positive tumors by IHC, while the eligibility section primarily describes tissue availability. Preserve this additional arm-level restriction and the differing enrollment totals.
extra_biomarker_requirement: Phase-arm descriptions require at least 50% DLL3 positivity by IHC; no individual result is established. Tissue availability alone is not equivalent to that positive result.
protocol_uncertainty: External protocol, adult non-SCLC investigator-discretion rules and live phase availability remain unverified. Metadata minimum age 18 omits the separately described pediatric neuroblastoma population, which does not create pediatric DSRCT access.
quotes: OR Desmoplastic small round cell tumors, osteosarcoma, Ewing's sarcoma, rabdomyosarcoma, Wilms tumors, hepatoblastomas, rhabdoid tumors and neuroblastoma patients

label: explicit_diagnosis_compatible
rationale: A dedicated Phase 2 DSRCT cohort requires consistent histology and EWSR1::WT1. Phase 1 permits sarcoma broadly, and the Other Sarcoma cohort expressly permits DSRCT with evaluable but nonmeasurable disease.
cohort_reconciliation: Do not apply the dedicated Phase 2 cohort's CNS-metastasis and prior irinotecan/temozolomide-progression exclusions to the entire study: the text limits them to EWS/DSRCT Phase 2 cohorts. Phase 1 and Other Sarcoma have separate CNS stability provisions and broader disease assessment scope. Dedicated slots for other histologies do not remove the express DSRCT route.
extra_biomarker_requirement: EWSR1::WT1 molecular confirmation is stated for the dedicated DSRCT cohort. It is distinct from the Ewing cohort's FET-ETS rule; no unrelated molecular gate is stated for the broad cohorts.
protocol_uncertainty: Ages 12–49, weight at least 40 kg, prior standard-therapy failure and other clinical requirements remain applicable. Insurance/self-pay agreement for temozolomide is an explicit access condition, not resolved here. Live phase/cohort capacity and external protocol are unverified.
quotes: Histologic diagnosis consistent with DSRCT; and
Molecular evidence of an EWSR1::WT1 fusion
Patients with EWS or DSRCT with evaluable but not measurable disease may participate in this cohort.
Patients who have had progressive disease while receiving irinotecan and temozolomide in combination will be excluded from the Phase 2 EWS and DSRCT cohorts only.

label: broad_tumor_compatible
rationale: Cohort D has open solid-tumor histologic scope for tumors outside Cohorts A–C, with mandatory patient-specific supporting evidence and principal-investigator approval. DSRCT is not expressly named; histologic compatibility does not establish the required evidence.
cohort_reconciliation: A–C are Wilms, rhabdoid and MPNST cohorts. D is the relevant open histologic route; E separately requires an activating BCOR alteration and is not inferred from DSRCT. Younger age groups have conditional PK enrollment and later Phase 2 entry, so metadata minimum age alone is insufficient.
extra_biomarker_requirement: Cohort D requires documented XPO1 dependency/activation/elevated expression or qualifying preclinical evidence plus PI approval; none is established by DSRCT. BCOR activation is a different cohort's gate and is likewise unestablished.
protocol_uncertainty: External protocol and PK/cohort availability are unverified. Prior systemic-treatment failure, measurable versus evaluable disease by phase, no prior XPO1 inhibitor and other clinical criteria remain applicable. Registry language suggesting benefit is an entry rationale, not demonstrated benefit.
quotes: Cohort D: Patients must not qualify for Cohorts A, B, or C but have a solid tumor (no hematologic malignancies including lymphoma) for which there is specific evidence that this particular patient's tumor may benefit from selinexor.
All patients in this cohort require approval of study principal investigator and must provide documentation of specific supporting evidence.
Cohort E: Patients must have a solid tumor with an activating genomic alteration (e.g. fusion or internal tandem duplication) involving BCOR.
